newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia to issue HRK300-500 mln Eurokuna in autumn.
newsitem.headline: Croatia to issue HRK300-500 mln Eurokuna in autumn.

text.p: Croatia plans a 300-500 million kuna Eurobond issue in domestic currency later in 1997 as part of the overall budget deficit of 2.8 billion kuna, Finance Minister Bozo Prka said on Thursday.

"It is realistic to expect the next issue of kuna-denominated bonds with a three-year, or perhaps even longer maturity in the autumn," Prka told Reuters in an interview. He declined to mention any other specifics.
"The price (of Croatian debt) on the secondary market is above par. So the interest on future issues will be falling," Prka said.
Croatia first tapped the Eurobond market for 300 million kuna in two-year bonds last December at a 12.5 percent annual interest.
"It was expensive money. But that was an admittance fee we had to pay to gain investor interest," Prka said.
High yield of the maiden issue helped to create much more demand for new debt than Croatia has at the moment, he added.
"With the Eurokuna, we practically tested the market and widened the range of instruments with which to finance the (budget) deficit."
The government has since raised $250 million in Eurodollar bonds, paying seven percent a year over five years. It also plans to issue German mark bonds in mid-year.
All the new borrowing goes for rebuilding the country after the 1991-95 war and for repaying the matured old debts.

Croatia was rated at the bottom of the investment grade ladder in January for the first time. But Prka saw a good chance of its sovereign rating improving with the normalisation in the former Yugoslavia.

"Out political neighbourhood was one of the key factors we were ranked relatively low... As the political situation improves, we shall soon gain conditions for upgrading the credit rating," he said. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
